sources.title: Mary Kingsley: Travels in West Africa, 1897
sources.note: Kangwe mission girls school paragraph; Ogooué journey poles and canoe crews; food preparation paragraph manioc troughs and leaf-wrapped rolls. Contemporary outsider with racist generalizations, which are not adopted.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: Eyema byeri, 1978.412.441
sources.note: Nineteenth-century Okak-Fang figure, Gabon or Equatorial Guinea. Bark containers, family/clan ancestors, material and separation from original assemblages.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: Ngombo, 1981.123
sources.note: Nineteenth-century Tsogo harp from Gabon; palm-fiber strings, small studs, skin belly, upright playing and women’s healing groups.

sources.title: François Uberfill: Helene Marianne Schweitzer-Bresslau
sources.note: 2006 scholarly biographical entry citing Schweitzer archives and correspondence. April 1913 Lambaréné arrival, hospital construction, responsible nurse; nursing training and documentary preparation.

sources.title: Bibliothèque nationale de France: Côte d’Ivoire before 1893
sources.note: Authority record identifies 10 March 1893 creation of French colony. Map 1878 precedes that administrative act.

sources.title: UNESCO: Historic Town of Grand-Bassam
sources.note: Description and outstanding universal value: specialised colonial quarters, N’zima fishing village, galleries/verandas/gardens, African-European-Levantine populations.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: Heddle pulley with elephant head
sources.note: 1978.412.289, nineteenth to mid-twentieth century, Baule Côte d’Ivoire. Narrow-band loom function, indigo-white cotton, carving and public display. Broad object date explicit.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: Comb with Rooster
sources.note: 1980.430, nineteenth to twentieth century, central Côte d’Ivoire, Baule, ivory and metal. No individual owner known.

sources.title: British Medical Journal: Yellow Fever in West Africa, 1911
sources.note: Printed page 305, sectionVIII Yellow fever on the Ivory Coast. Primary historical report on 1899 to 1905 outbreaks,1903 shipping interruption and change from house-burning to drainage/antimosquito measures. Indexed PDF text read; direct opening failed. Not contemporary medical advice.

sources.title: Christophe Wondji: Bingerville, naissance d’une capitale,1899 to 1909
sources.note: 1976 original archival historical research, pages 83 to 102; page 85 read and abstract indexed. Colonial economic motives, conflict with Ebrie residents and 1903 insurrection.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: Geometric gold weight,1994.312.3
sources.note: Enid Schildkrout 2025 essay, brass and lost-wax casting. Object dated 16th to 17th century, geography Ghana/Côte d’Ivoire uncertain. Used explicitly as older regional background, not a colonial invention.

sources.title: US Office of the Historian: Côte d’Ivoire
sources.note: Recognition and independence 7 August 1960; ending distinguishes 1914 map cutoff.

batchIdentityNotes.assessment: Imported 1878 to 1914 snapshots include coastal footprint, not identical to modern republic. Separate later gabon-1945 card retained. Museum examples explicitly dated and cross-border attribution disclosed; no modern WASH data retrojected.

Imported 1878 to 1914 coastal footprint. Formal colony 1893 and independence 1960 distinguished; modern ivory-coast-1960 remains separate. Baule examples clearly regional with broad 19th to 20th-century dates; older Akan weight explicitly background, uncertain Ghana/IvoryCoast provenance. No inferred uniform schooling or sanitation.
